The Arrival

It has stood here
since before the columns
were raised.

Neo-Georgian. Longitudinal plan. Columned portico. Circular drive. The proportions are correct because the original drawings survived.

Built by Leonard Tufts' own craftsmen.

The same men
who built Pinehurst.

He named it. He directed every brick from London.
He came home in 1918 and was gone ten days later.

"Well, Frank, I did get here after all, didn't I?"

The house outlasted him by a century.
That was always the point.

Every house needs someone equal to it.

In 1959, she arrived.

Act IV

Betty Dumaine.

She arrived in 1959 and renamed it Hollycrest.
That is the kind of woman she was.

She kept peacocks. She threw birthday parties for her horse.
Her closest friend was the Princess Mother of Thailand.

For twenty-five years, this was the address in Pinehurst.

She died in 1984. The house stood empty for fourteen years.

Nothing needed to be touched.

The Foyer

The brass key plates
still have their original keys.

The oak floors are the ones they put down first.

The door has been open since 1916.

The Staircase

The curve was not necessary.

They put it in anyway.

The Salon

They made it bigger
so they could dance.

Seven windows. A fireplace that has held every kind of evening. The proportions are not accidental.

This room was always meant for more than furniture.

The Drawing Room

Fire going.
No one home yet.

The coffered ceiling. The Georgian mantel.
The Delft tile surround — blue and white, Dutch, exact.

This is the room you find yourself returning to.

The Dining Room

The chandelier has presided
over a century of meals.

The fireplace is original.
Twelve can sit here without crowding.
More, if the occasion demands it.

The Kitchen

Not original to the house.
Original to the restoration.

A wall of windows over the sink.
The kind of light that makes the whole room feel like morning.

The Library

The spiral stair
is not decorative.

It goes somewhere.
Floor to ceiling. A fireplace at one end.
The kind of room that makes you want to stay in on a Saturday.

The Primary Suite

Four poster. High ceilings.
Morning light from the east.

Designed for privacy within a house built for gathering.
You feel the difference the moment the door closes.

The second floor is where the house exhales.

Three additional bedrooms. Each one different.
Each one quiet in its own way.

Now they are
a forest.

The Grounds

4.15 acres.
The world outside
does not exist here.

The pool is southwest. Tennis courts northeast — ready for restoration. The rear of the house opens entirely to the grounds through glass.

At the back of the grounds there is a small stone marker.

MY IRISH HUNTER  ·  BLUE FOX  ·  1946 – 1965

Betty Dumaine lived here for twenty-five years.
She kept peacocks. She knew the Princess Mother of Thailand.
She renamed this house Hollycrest and made it the address in Pinehurst.

Someone still puts flowers there.

Garran Hill is ready.
It is offered now for the first time.

The question is whether you are.
